notes:
Passed on the fake backend by python3 -m mhs.driver check (evidence contract_checked, never an MHS-Device level). Model-authored and unreviewed (driver.lock.json reviewed_by null); no hardware was attached or run and the driver has no hardware backend. The upstream clone was never imported, installed or run: its README.md:74 documents Linux/Windows only and compiled *.so/*.dll libraries. The fake is an F0 analytic stand-in for FlyCraftEnv: it mirrors the observation/action spaces of the default guidance_law_mode configuration, the reset/step protocol and the timeout truncation, but not the F16 flight model, control law, upstream reward/termination set, numpy goal sampler or end_to_end_mode; the fidelity gaps and fake.py placeholders say so. The card lists flycraft.env_level_turn:FlyCraftLevelTurnEnv as a second entry symbol; this package serves the primary FlyCraft-v0 (flycraft.env:FlyCraftEnv) and does not cover the level-turn variant. No catalogue requests: only cap.world.step.v1, cap.world.reset.v1 and cap.world.seed.v1 are used, all served by the Gymnasium family. Expected warnings only: G6.NO_NATIVE_CALL for cap.world.seed.v1 (the seed sets the next reset and makes no native call) and four G8.NO_UNIT for the bridge-derived integer/numeric inputs (seed in reset, seed in seed, ticks, action.values); there were no G4.REF_VALUE or G4.REF_BINARY warnings. gate.digest is the digest line the check printed (the report without its clock); check-report.json is regenerated by every gate run and is not part of the package.
